references.text: Describes how the sacrificial animal was to be skinned and cut into pieces as part of the burnt offering ritual
The entrails and feet were to be washed with water before being offered on the altar, following the same procedure as in Exodus 29:17
The animal was to be cut into pieces, and the entrails and feet washed with water, parallel to the consecration offering
Moses carried out what was commanded in Exodus 29—the ram was cut into pieces and its entrails and feet were washed
The burnt offering with the pieces and the head, along with washed entrails and feet, follows the same pattern
Earlier in the same chapter, the entrails are mentioned in connection with the sin offering, as part of the same consecration ritual
Lev 1:12 confirms the general rule for preparing the burnt offering (cutting into pieces and handling the head) that is specified for the ram in Ex 29.
Lev 9:14 documents that Moses performed the specific washing and burning commanded in Ex 29.
Lev 1:13 repeats the general law regarding the washing of entrails, as followed in Ex 29:17.
Both verses belong to the same confirmation offering ceremony (the ordination offering) in Exodus 29.
Lev 8:21 documents that Moses performed the specific washing and burning of the ram as commanded in Ex 29.
